title: How to Fix Common Audio Problems in Windows 10? - GeeksforGeeks
content:
Having trouble with the sound on your Windows 10 device can be irritating, particularly when you're in a meeting, watching a video, or listening to music. This manual will guide you through resolving typical sound problems in Windows 10, including easy troubleshooting steps to get your sound system up and running again.

How to Fix Common Audio Problems in Windows 10?

Table of Content

  • How to Fix Common Audio Problems in Windows 10?
    • Method 1: Check all the Audio Connections
    • Method 2: Restart your System
    • Method 3: Restart the Windows Audio Services
    • Method 4: Run the Automatic Audio Troubleshoot
    • Method 5: Check the Default Input and Output for Audio
    • Method 6: Update the IDT High Definition Audio CODEC
    • Method 7: Disable the Audio Enhancements

Given below are the methods to fix common audio problems in Windows 10.

Method 1: Check all the Audio Connections

Securely and correctly plug in your speakers or headphones. For wireless devices, confirm they're paired and connected to your system.

Step 1: Connect your speakers or headphones properly.

Step 2: Inspect the wires, plugs, volume, speaker, and headphone connections.

Step 3: Connect them to another device to rule out any hardware issues.

Method 2: Restart your System

Resolve seemingly unsolvable issues, like temporary software glitches affecting audio, by restarting your PC. Close all applications, restart your computer, and see if the problem continues.

  • Press and hold the power button for 5-10 seconds.
  • Wait 30 seconds, then press the power button again.

Method 3: Restart the Windows Audio Services

Windows audio services manage the audio devices and processes on your system. However, these services can sometimes stop working or malfunction, leading to audio problems.

To solve follow the given steps to fix the audio issue in Windows:

Step 1: Press Win + R to open the Run dialog box.

Step 2: Type services. msc and press Enter.

Step 3: Scroll down and find Windows Audio Services.

Step 4: Right-click and select Restart.

Method 4: Run the Automatic Audio Troubleshoot

It will check all major audio settings and installed drivers, either resolving the issue or identifying the exact problem for you.

Step 1: Open the Settings app by pressing Windows Key + I

Step 2: Go to the System section.

Step 3: Click on Sound.

Step 4: Click on Troubleshoot.

Method 5: Check the Default Input and Output for Audio

It might be incorrect or incompatible audio settings that are causing your audio issues. Maybe you had the wrong audio input or output device, or the wrong sample rate or bit depth was set. To rectify this, check and adjust the default input and output for audio.

Follow these steps to fix common audio problems in Windows 10:

Step 1: Open the Settings app by pressing Windows Key + I

Step 2: Go to the System section.

Step 3: Click on Sound.

Step 4: From "Input" and "Output" select the default output device and ensure it is connected and functioning properly on your computer.

Method 6: Update the IDT High Definition Audio CODEC

To fix common audio problems in Windows 10, you may need to update the IDT High Definition Audio CODEC. This is how your computer manages audio devices. Follow these steps:

Step 1: Press Win + S, then type "Device Manager" into the search bar.

Step 2: Expand the "Sound, Video, and Game Controllers" section.

Step 3: Right-click on "High Definition Audio Device" and select "Update Driver".

Step 4: Restart Your system

Method 7: Disable the Audio Enhancements

Audio enhancements, while designed to improve your audio’s quality and performance, can sometimes lead to compatibility issues or conflicts with certain audio devices or applications. To address this, consider disabling the audio enhancements.

Step 1: Right Click on " System Tray" and then select "Sounds"

Step 2: in Headphones properties, navigate to the "Playback" tab

Step 3: Then, Select "Properties"

Step 4: In the next window, navigate to the "Enhancements" tab.

Step 5: Check the box labeled "Disable all enhancements" then click on the "Apply" button

Step 6: Click on OK

In the end, Solving sound issues in Windows 10 isn't always difficult. With these instructions, you can diagnose and resolve the majority of audio problems, bringing back the ability to hear and ensuring your device operates without interruption.
